parameters.name: request_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the requests with the student, the reason, the proposed slot and the status.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Why it is being closed. It sits on the record beside the concern the teacher raised.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: The request.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Closed. It stays on the record (BR-9).

fields.name: reason
fields.description: As given.

fields.name: offers_made
fields.description: How many slots were offered.

fields.description: What the family said each time, including silence.

fields.name: days_unanswered
fields.description: How long it went without a response, where it did (BR-8).

fields.name: visible_to_coordinator
fields.description: True. A family not engaging is something the school needs to see (BR-8).

fields.name: concern_unresolved
fields.description: True. The teacher raised something and the meeting did not happen.

errors.meaning: A request was closed with no reason.
The request is already closed or terminal.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. It sits on the record beside the concern the teacher raised, and it is what a coordinator reads when deciding whether a family is being avoided or simply unavailable.
Report that the concern is unresolved. The teacher raised something a family needed to know about and the meeting did not happen — closing the request does not close that (BR-8).

Report the history plainly: how many slots were offered, what the family said each time, and how long it went unanswered. That record is the only thing that distinguishes a family with a difficult week from one avoiding the school (BR-8, BR-9).

Say that nothing acts on the visibility. What a coordinator does about a family that repeatedly does not engage is not decided anywhere in this use case, so closing it puts the matter in a list nobody is required to do anything with.
Never delete a request instead of closing it. A declined, closed or unanswered request stays on the record, which is what makes a pattern visible (BR-9, E9).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A closure is not undone. A teacher who wants to try again raises a fresh request, and both stay on the record (BR-9).

Then ask what the reason should say: how long it went unanswered is part of the record, and after how many days one is surfaced to the coordinator is not decided anywhere.

operations.name: stock.item.create
operations.idempotencyKey: name + category + branch, so a double press does not leave two items for one shelf
operations.purpose: Create a stock item with its unit, reorder level and type.

parameters.name: name
parameters.notes: 2 to 100 characters, unique within its category (BR-6, E1). Two entries for the same thing is two balances for one shelf.

parameters.name: category_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No such category. Who maintains the category list, and whether one may be created while creating an item, is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-1).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the categories that match.

parameters.notes: What kind of item it is. Lists and counts group by it.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.notes: The unit the item is counted in (E2). **Fixed once anything moves against the item** — changing it would make every past receipt, issue and count mean something different from what it meant when it was recorded (BR-2, E5, AC-5).

parameters.name: reorder_level
parameters.notes: Zero or more (E3). The quantity at which the item must be bought again. A standing commitment to buy rather than a description, which is why only the School Admin sets it (BR-3, E4, AC-4).

parameters.name: item_type
parameters.notes: A consumable is used up once issued. A returnable is expected back and **stays outstanding against the person who took it** until it is returned (BR-4, AC-6, AC-7). Never guessed from the item's name.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The item and what it now permits.

fields.name: item_id
fields.description: The item.

fields.name: name
fields.description: As entered, unique within its category.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: What it is counted in, from here on and permanently (BR-2).

fields.name: reorder_level
fields.description: The level at which it is flagged for buying (BR-7).

fields.name: item_type
fields.description: Consumable or returnable, which decides whether an issue of it ever closes (BR-4).

fields.name: on_hand
fields.description: Zero. The quantity comes from receipts, issues and counts and is never typed (BR-5, E6).

fields.name: available_for
fields.description: Requests, receipts, issues and counts (AC-1).

errors.meaning: An item of the same name already exists in that category.
errors.note: Two entries called the same thing in one category is how a store ends up with two balances for one shelf (BR-6, AC-2).

errors.meaning: No unit was selected.
No reorder level was set.
errors.note: It is what triggers buying the item again (BR-3, AC-3).

errors.meaning: A member of staff attempted to set the reorder level.
errors.note: A reorder level commits the school to buying, so it sits with the School Admin and not with whoever holds the store (BR-3, AC-4).

planningRules.rule: Never guess the unit. It is fixed the moment anything moves against the item and cannot be changed afterwards by any route (BR-2, E5, AC-5) — a marker counted in boxes and a marker counted in pieces are the same shelf and two different balances. Ask which.

Never guess consumable or returnable. It decides whether an issue of the item ever closes: a returnable stays outstanding against the person who took it, a consumable does not (BR-4, AC-6, AC-7). A projector remote read as a consumable is an item nobody is ever asked to bring back.
Never set or suggest a reorder level of your own. It is a standing commitment to buy, it belongs to the School Admin, and a level nobody chose is a purchasing decision nobody made (BR-3, BR-8, E4).
Never offer to set the quantity on hand. There is no such field — the balance comes from receipts, issues and counts (BR-5, E6, AC-9).

Check the name against the category before creating. A near-duplicate is refused only on an exact match, and "Marker, black" beside "Whiteboard marker, black" passes the check and splits the shelf in two (BR-1, BR-6).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An item created in error is deactivated with a reason and stays readable, because receipts, issues and counts reference it (BR-9, E8). There is no deletion. An item with the wrong unit cannot be corrected at all once it is in use — it is deactivated and a new one created, so past counts keep their meaning (A4).

Say who a reorder-level change binds. It is a standing commitment to buy, it is recorded with the name of whoever moved it, and it takes effect the moment the balance crosses it (BR-3, BR-7, BR-8, A5).

Say what a change of type does not do. Turning a consumable into a returnable does not open the issues already made, and turning a returnable into a consumable does not close the ones outstanding — it applies from here on, and the items already out stay exactly as they were (BR-4, BR-5).

operations.name: session.end

planningRules.rule: session_id always comes from $session. A request naming another person, another device or another campus is not a sign-out this plan can perform — it is account suspension (UC-25-01) or something the system does not offer (OQ-1). Never lift a session id out of the request.
Never emit this step in the same plan as anything else. It invalidates the session every later step depends on, and every subsequent operation returns E3. A sign-out is always the whole plan.
Never plan a sign-out to clear a failed write, discard a half-finished form, or reset state. Unsaved data is discarded without a prompt (BR-4) and nothing already written is rolled back by it.
reason is the literal user, never a value from the request. A timeout end is written by the session service; a plan that claims one falsifies the audit log.

Never name the application in the plan. The session already identifies whether it is a driver session or a main-system one, and a driver sign-out must not touch a main-system session held by the same person.
Never re-emit the step after SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED. It is the success path, not a retryable failure.

reversal.statement: There is no un-sign-out. A session is recreated only by signing in at /login, which is UC-01-01 and carries no planning contract. The controller must not attempt a compensating call, and must not offer to sign the actor back in.

planningRules.rule: branch_id and session_id come from $session in every step, even where the request names a campus or a past year. A request for another branch's figures is not a parameter change; it is a branch switch the actor makes in the header, and a planner that passes it as a parameter is reaching across a scope boundary the whole convention exists to hold.

Never name a tile in the call. There is no parameter for it, and a request asking after one figure produces the same plan as a request asking after all of them. This is what keeps BR-2 true: an unpermitted figure is absent from the response, and an absence discloses nothing, where a refusal would confirm the figure exists.

Never re-emit the call with the failing figure excluded to obtain a clean set. There is no parameter that would exclude it, and an unavailable figure is the answer for that figure.
Every figure is quoted with its calculated_at. A number repeated an hour later without its timestamp is the failure BR-5 exists to prevent.
Where is_historical is true, the figures are as at the session's close and must be reported that way. Never present a historical figure as the current position.
Never add a refresh step to make a figure newer. Refresh is a screen action on an open dashboard; a plan calculates once.

resolvedPlans.request: show me the library summary
resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, library module carrying two meaningful figures.

steps.note: Resolution returns module_key library. The capability then returns returned_as list, because the module carries fewer than three meaningful figures (BR-11, A4). The plan neither predicted this nor branched on it.

steps.note: One step. The filters behind the figure are applied by the backend from the figure_key — they are never carried in the plan, so there is no way for a planner to edit them and produce a list that looks like proof and is not.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A figure the role may not see fails at resolution, before the plan runs. A figure that resolves but whose rows are refused arrives as an error from the call — a real state, in which the number is visible and the rows are not.
plan.atomicity: One read. Nothing is written except the audit entry the API makes for a financial figure, so a run whose rows are refused has still recorded the viewing.

operations.name: dashboard.drilldown.read
operations.purpose: Return the rows a dashboard figure was calculated from, with the figure's own filters applied by the backend, so the number can be proved. The filters never pass through the AI layer, which is what makes the list add up.

parameters.name: figure_key

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No permitted figure matches the words used. A figure the role may not see is indistinguishable from one that does not exist, which is BR-2 working.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates. Never pick one.

parameters.notes: An entity id, obtained by the parameter resolver through the resolve door from the words the actor used for the figure. Resolution matches within the role's permitted set only, so a figure the actor may not see never resolves (BR-2).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope, BR-4).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope, BR-4).

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.notes: The default page size under the list-screens convention. total_count carries the full figure regardless of the page.

returns.description: The rows behind the figure, the figure as calculated, and their totals — so the two can be reconciled in one response.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: The list's own columns, as defined by the module that owns it.

fields.name: total_count
fields.description: The full count under the figure's filters.

fields.name: total_value
fields.description: Present on money lists. Should reconcile with figure_value (AC-3).

fields.name: figure_value
fields.description: The figure as calculated, returned alongside its rows so a mismatch is visible without a second call.

fields.name: figure_calculated_at
fields.description: When the figure was calculated (BR-5).

fields.name: filters_applied
fields.description: Echoed back for the reply, not for the plan. The AI layer never sets these.

fields.name: list_name
fields.description: The list's name, for quoting back.

errors.meaning: The actor may see the figure but may not open the list behind it.
errors.note: Message: "You do not have permission to view this record." Report the figure and that the rows are out of reach. Do not retry with fewer filters.

errors.meaning: The filters match no rows.
errors.note: A genuine answer where the figure is zero. Where the figure is not zero, an empty list is a reconciliation problem worth reporting, not a run to retry.

operations.writesOnRead: Reading a financial figure's rows writes the same audit entry as calculating it, because the value is returned with them.

planningRules.rule: Carry the phrase, never a key. figure_key is $request.figure_phrase and the resolver converts it. Resolution matches only within the permitted set, so a planner that writes a key directly walks past the permission that resolution is enforcing.

Never put filters in the plan. There is no parameter for them. The backend applies the figure's own filters from the figure_key, which is what guarantees the list reconciles with the number — a guarantee that disappears the moment a planner can name a filter.
Never add a step to open a list yourself. There is one capability here, and it returns the rows and the figure together.
Never raise page_size to return more rows. total_count already carries the full figure, and the page is a display concern.
Never re-emit the call after a refusal of the rows. FORBIDDEN_LIST means the actor may see the figure and not the rows behind it, which is an answer about their permissions, not a call to retry.
Where total_count does not reconcile with figure_value, report both with the timestamp. Never quote one as the other. The two arrive in the same response precisely so the drift is visible.
Never chain an action onto this plan. It returns rows to read; messaging them, exporting them or changing them are separate use cases with contracts of their own.

Hand the resolver the words the actor used for the figure, in the language they used them. "jinhon ne fees nahi di" names the defaulters figure as plainly as the word defaulters does. Never translate it into a figure key, and never infer the key from the module the figure sits in.
branch_id and session_id come from $session, even where the request names a campus or a past year. Scope is not a parameter a request can set.

reversal.statement: Both operations are reads. Nothing is written except the audit entry for viewing a financial figure, which is never editable under the audit-trail convention. There is no compensating call.

steps.note: The only step. record_type and include_inactive are omitted entirely unless the request asks for them; the API defaults them to All and false.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The minimum length, the row scope and the role's right to search at all are enforced by the API and arrive as errors; the plan does not test for them beforehand. Nothing matching is not a failure — it is the answer (E2).
plan.atomicity: One step. No student or staff record is created, changed or deactivated. One thing is written: the audit entry recording the term searched (BR-9), so even a run that returns nothing leaves a record that the search happened. That entry is never editable and is not something the controller can undo.

operations.name: search.global
operations.purpose: Match a name or a system-issued number against student and staff records inside the actor's role and branch scope, and return up to twenty of them with the total.

parameters.name: q
parameters.notes: The name or number only — the span of the sentence that names the person, never the sentence itself. "Ahmed Raza ko dhoondo" gives q "Ahmed Raza" (PR-10). Passed exactly as given: never re-spelled, transliterated or translated (PR-11). Minimum 3 characters; trimmed, case- and accent-insensitive. Matches name, roll number, student ID and staff ID only (BR-3) — never a guardian's mobile, an address or a date of birth.

parameters.name: record_type
parameters.notes: Only where the sentence names the type outright — "find the teacher Nadia" is Staff. A form of address is not a type: madam, sir and baji narrow nothing (PR-12). Omit otherwise; the API defaults to All. Narrowing is safe from a permissions view because it never widens what the role may see (BR-1), but a wrong narrowing still hides the person.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.notes: True only where the request states the person has gone — "chala gaya tha", "TC ho gaya", "left last year" (PR-13). Never set true to widen a search that returned nothing — see PR-3.

parameters.name: branch_scope
parameters.notes: The branches this role may reach. Never from the request, even where the request names a campus. Global search widens reach across modules, never across permissions (BR-1).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: The academic session held in controller context (academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Up to twenty matches, each carrying what it takes to tell two people apart, plus the full total.

fields.name: matches
fields.description: record_type, record_id, name, class_or_department, roll_or_staff_number, status, branch_name, is_inactive. record_type and branch_name must be reported with each match (BR-4, BR-10).

fields.name: total_count
fields.description: How many matched in total, which may exceed the number shown (BR-6).

fields.name: shown_count
fields.description: Never more than twenty.

fields.name: full_list_key
fields.description: The student or staff list carrying the same term, where the total exceeds twenty (A1).

fields.name: scope_note
fields.description: What was searched in words — "Johar Town branch", "All branches", "Grade 1 and 2". Reported with the results so an empty answer is readable.

errors.meaning: Fewer than three characters were submitted.
errors.written: Nothing. No search ran, so no audit entry either.
errors.note: On screen no search runs and the panel does not open. Ask for more of the name rather than searching on two letters.

errors.meaning: Nothing in scope matches the term.
errors.written: The audit entry for the term searched (BR-9).
errors.note: Message: "No student or staff member matches that." This is the answer, not a failure. Never retried with include_inactive true or a shortened term.

errors.meaning: The search took longer than 10 seconds and was abandoned.
errors.written: Nothing reliable. The audit entry may or may not have been written.
errors.note: Message: "Search is taking longer than usual. Try a fuller name or a roll number." Report it; do not silently retry.

errors.meaning: The role may not use global search at all — Teacher, Student, Parent / Guardian and Driver.
errors.note: On screen the search box is not rendered in the header. A Teacher reaches their students through their class lists, which is the narrower and safer path.

operations.writesOnRead: Every search writes one audit entry naming the actor, the term and the time (BR-9), because this feature reaches personal data across the whole school. The entry recording which record was opened is written by whichever use case opens it, not by this plan.

planningRules.rule: Never chain a profile open onto this search, not even where exactly one record matches. A single result is reported for the actor to confirm, never opened for them (A2). The plan ends at the matches.
branch_scope comes from $session. A request naming a campus outside the actor's scope does not widen the search — it returns nothing, and that is correct. Never pass a branch from the request.

Never re-emit the search with include_inactive set true because it returned nothing. Inactive records are included only where the request asks for a former, left or struck-off person. A struck-off student surfacing unasked is how one gets mistaken for an enrolled one.
Never shorten, generalise or re-spell the term to find something. A search that matches nothing is the answer (E2), and a broadened one returns people nobody asked about.

Never put a guardian's mobile, an address, a date of birth or a parent's name in q. Only names and system-issued identifiers are matched (BR-3), and the use case's own open question records that a guardian's number has not been agreed as matchable.
Never plan this to enumerate. A term built to sweep a class, a department or a whole branch — "Grade 5", "Khan" to list every Khan — is a list, and lists are out of scope here.

Report each match with its record_type, and with branch_name where the scope spans branches. Dropping either is exactly how a student and a staff member of the same name, or two pupils of the same name at two campuses, get confused.
Where total_count exceeds shown_count, say so and offer the full list. Presenting twenty of sixty as the answer is a wrong answer.
Never emit this step to check whether a person exists before some other action. The audit log records every term searched, and a search run to probe is a search that will be read back later as one.

Put into q only the span that names the person, never the sentence around it. "Ahmed Raza ko dhoondo" searches for "Ahmed Raza"; ko dhoondo is grammar. A sentence passed whole matches nothing and reads afterwards, in the audit log, as a search nobody would have typed.

Never re-spell, transliterate or translate a name or a system-issued identifier. The record holds the spelling it was registered with, in Latin script, and Ayesha, Aisha and Ayeshah are three different searches. Where a name arrives in Urdu script, ask for it as it appears on the record rather than rendering it into Latin — a rendering is a guess with a person's identity in it. Eastern Arabic digits inside an identifier are normalised to Latin digits, which changes the script and not the number.

Set record_type only where the sentence names the type outright. Ustaad, sir, madam and baji are forms of address as often as they are job descriptions, and a wrong narrowing hides the person being looked for. Where it is not stated plainly, omit record_type and let All match — the record type comes back on every row anyway.

Read include_inactive from what the request states, not from how it is phrased. "Chala gaya tha", "TC ho gaya" and "left last year" all state that the person has gone; a wistful past tense does not. Where it is unclear, leave the flag off and report that nothing matched — PR-3 already forbids widening it afterwards.

reversal.statement: A search creates, changes and deactivates nothing, so there is nothing to reverse. The audit entry it writes is deliberate and never editable under the audit-trail convention — the controller must not attempt to remove or amend it.

steps.note: One step, and all of it is required. A branch missing its logo, its bank account or its first administrator is not created at all — each of the three is something the rest of the system reads from it (BR-2, BR-3, BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A duplicate name or code, a missing logo or letterhead, no bank account, or no first administrator each refuses the whole creation. Nothing half-made is left behind.
plan.atomicity: One act: the branch, its branding, its bank account, its first Principal or School Admin, and the seal. **The branch is sealed from the moment it exists** — its Principal and School Admin see nothing of any other campus, and only the Super Admin holds visibility across branches (BR-5).

operations.name: branch.create
operations.idempotencyKey: branch code, since a code is unique and a double press must not create two campuses the system cannot tell apart
operations.purpose: Create a branch with its branding, bank account and first administrator.

parameters.name: name
parameters.notes: 2 to 100 characters, unique. Two branches sharing a name is two campuses the system cannot tell apart (BR-8, E1).

parameters.name: code
parameters.notes: A short code in uppercase letters and hyphens, unique. **It goes into every reference number the branch issues**, so it is not a label — it is part of every challan, certificate and identifier that campus will ever produce (BR-8, E1).

parameters.name: address
parameters.notes: 10 to 500 characters. Printed on the documents the branch issues.

parameters.name: contact
parameters.notes: The branch telephone number and email.

parameters.name: logo_file_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No uploaded file matches. The logo is attached on the screen first.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this branch.

parameters.notes: The branch's own logo. Required (BR-2, E2) — a certificate from one campus should not go out on another's letterhead. Uploaded on the screen first; a file cannot travel in a plan.

parameters.name: letterhead_file_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No uploaded file matches. The letterhead is attached on the screen first.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this branch.

parameters.notes: The branch's own letterhead, carried by the certificates and letters it issues (BR-2, E2).

parameters.name: bank_account
parameters.notes: The branch's own account. Required (BR-3, E3) — **fee challans and online payments for this branch are directed to it**, and fee money must arrive at the campus that charged it.

parameters.name: first_administrator
parameters.notes: The person seeded with the branch so it has somebody able to staff it. Required (BR-4, E4) — a branch with nobody able to assign users cannot be populated at all.

parameters.name: administrator_role
parameters.notes: Either Principal / Director or School Admin. The use case names the two in prose and declares no value list on the field, so they are carried as written rather than as an enum. Which of the two the first administrator holds. Either is acceptable; what matters is that the branch has somebody able to staff it (BR-4, A1).

returns.description: The branch and what it now controls.

fields.name: branch_id
fields.description: The branch. Every record in the system will carry it (BR-1).

fields.name: code
fields.description: What every reference number the branch issues will carry (BR-8).

fields.name: documents_carry
fields.description: The logo and letterhead this campus's certificates, cards and letters will be issued on (BR-2).

fields.name: fee_money_goes_to
fields.description: The bank account challans and online payments for this branch are directed to (BR-3).

fields.name: first_administrator
fields.description: Who was seeded, and in which role. Every user after this is assigned by the branch itself (BR-4, E5).

fields.name: sealed
fields.description: True, from creation. The branch's Principal and School Admin see nothing of any other — not its students, staff, fees, ledger, timetable or reports (BR-5).

fields.name: cross_branch_visibility
fields.description: The Super Admin only. Nobody else holds it by default (BR-5, BR-6).

fields.name: boundary_exceptions
fields.description: The only two, both scoped and temporary: a transfer in progress, and an employee assigned to more than one branch. **Neither is a written use case** — UC-23-05 and UC-23-06 are named and do not exist (BR-9).

errors.meaning: A branch of the same name or code exists.
errors.note: Two branches sharing either is two campuses the system cannot tell apart (BR-8).

errors.meaning: No logo or letterhead was uploaded.
errors.note: The branch's documents carry them (BR-2).

errors.meaning: No bank account was recorded.
errors.note: Fee money for this branch is directed to it (BR-3).

errors.meaning: No first administrator was seeded.
errors.note: It needs somebody able to staff it (BR-4).

planningRules.rule: Never invent a branch code. It goes into every reference number the campus will ever issue — challans, certificates, identifiers — so it is not a label to be filled in helpfully, and it cannot be changed afterwards without breaking every reference already issued (BR-8, E1).

Never proceed without the bank account. Fee money for this branch is directed to it, and a campus created without one either cannot issue a challan or issues it against somebody else's account (BR-3, E3).
Never substitute another campus's logo or letterhead. A certificate from one campus going out on another's is exactly what the rule exists to stop (BR-2, E2).

Say that the Super Admin seeds one person and no more. Every user after the first is assigned by the branch's own School Admin, and a Super Admin who keeps assigning has taken over the operational work the design keeps away from them (BR-4, E5).

Say what sealed means before it surprises anybody. The new branch's Principal will see nothing of any other campus — not its students, staff, fees, ledger, timetable or reports — and nobody sees across branches without the Super Admin granting it deliberately (BR-5, BR-6, E6).

Name the two exceptions to the seal and say that neither exists yet. A transfer in progress and an employee at more than one branch are the only things that cross the boundary, and the use cases for both are named and unwritten (BR-9).

reversal.statement: A branch created in error is deactivated with a reason — and only once its students and staff have been transferred or exited (BR-7, BR-10, E8). It is never deleted, because its students, staff, ledger entries and audit trail all reference it (E9).

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin.

steps.note: All of it is required; four things are missing and each blocks the creation (PR-2, PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Ask for the address, the contact, the logo and letterhead, and the bank account before anything is created — none is optional, and the bank account is the one that matters most: every challan this campus issues is directed to it. Confirm the code, since it goes into every reference number the branch will ever produce. After: report that the campus is sealed, that Dr Malik will see nothing of any other branch, and that every user after her is assigned by her own School Admin rather than by the Super Admin.

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, with LHR-JT already in use by Johar Town.

steps.note: Refused on the code before anything else is asked (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is created. LHR-JT belongs to the Johar Town campus, and two branches sharing a code is two campuses the system cannot tell apart — every reference number either issues would be ambiguous. Ask for a different code, and note that it cannot be changed later without orphaning every reference already issued under it.

steps.note: One step, and neither the name nor the code is among the parameters — the code is embedded in every reference the branch has issued (BR-8).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Clearing the logo, the letterhead or the bank account is refused like leaving it out at creation — the branch's documents and its fee money depend on all three (E2, E3).
plan.atomicity: One write. Everything issued **from now on** carries the new branding and is directed to the new account; nothing already issued changes (BR-2, BR-3).

operations.name: branch.update
operations.idempotencyKey: branch_id + the fields submitted, so a double press does not record the same change twice
operations.purpose: Change a branch's address, contact, branding or bank account.

parameters.name: branch_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No branch matches that name or code.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the branches that match with their codes and whether each is active.

parameters.notes: The branch, named by its campus name or its code.

parameters.name: address
parameters.notes: The corrected address, printed on the branch's documents.

parameters.name: contact
parameters.notes: The branch telephone number and email.

parameters.name: logo_file_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No uploaded file matches. The logo is attached on the screen first.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this branch.

parameters.notes: A replacement logo. Cannot be cleared — the branch's documents carry it (BR-2, E2).

parameters.name: letterhead_file_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No uploaded file matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this branch.

parameters.notes: A replacement letterhead (BR-2, E2).

parameters.name: bank_account
parameters.notes: A replacement account. **Every challan issued after this is directed to it** — challans already out carry the old one (BR-3, E3).

returns.description: What changed and what it changes from here on.

fields.name: branch_id
fields.description: The branch.

fields.name: changed
fields.description: Field by field, from and to, with who changed it.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Unchanged. It is not a parameter — every reference number the branch has issued carries it (BR-8).

fields.name: documents_from_now
fields.description: New branding applies to documents issued from this point. Certificates and cards already issued carry the old logo and letterhead (BR-2).

fields.name: challans_from_now
fields.description: New account applies to challans issued from this point. Challans already out still name the old account, and a family paying against one of those pays into it (BR-3).

fields.name: outstanding_challans
fields.description: Challans already issued and unpaid against the previous account. Nothing reissues them.

errors.meaning: The logo or letterhead was cleared rather than replaced.
errors.note: The branch's documents carry them (BR-2).

errors.meaning: The bank account was cleared rather than replaced.
errors.note: Fee money for this branch is directed to it (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Say that a change of bank account does not reissue anything. Every challan already out names the old account and a family paying against one of those pays into it — the school has to decide what happens to those, and nothing here does (BR-3).
Say that new branding applies from here on. Certificates and cards already issued carry the old logo and letterhead permanently, and nothing reissues them (BR-2).
Never attempt the code. It is embedded in every reference number the branch has issued and is not a parameter of this operation (BR-8).
Never clear a required field. A branch with no letterhead or no account is one the creation rules would have refused, and editing is not the way round that (BR-2, BR-3, E2, E3).

reversal.statement: There is no undo. A further correction is another change, and documents issued in between carry whatever was current at the time — which is the point of recording what changed and when.

request.text: Johar Town ka bank account badal dein, naya HBL wala account hai
request.gloss: change Johar Town's bank account, the new one is the HBL account

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, 214 challans issued and unpaid against the old account.

steps.note: One step. It is the Super Admin's decision and nobody holds it by default (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A grant by anybody other than the Super Admin is refused outright (E7).
plan.atomicity: One write. It does not unseal anything else: the branches stay sealed to everybody else, and this one person sees consolidated figures across the branches named (BR-5, BR-6).

operations.name: branch.consolidatedview.grant

planningRules.rule: Never act on another account. This is the acting user's own profile setting; requiring a factor of somebody else is an enforcement and belongs to the Super Admin (BR-1, BR-2).
Say that enabling has not enrolled anything. Until the user enrols a factor themselves, a password alone still signs them in — which is the exact gap this control exists to close (BR-3, BR-5).
Never carry a confirming code. Enrolment matches a code against an authenticator and a code is a credential — it never travels through a plan, and nobody enrols on anybody's behalf (BR-3, E2).
Say plainly what disabling gives up. A password on its own becomes enough again, and that is the whole point of the second step (BR-5).
Where it is enforced, say so rather than reporting a failure. It is required for their role and is not theirs to change — the refusal is the design (BR-1, E1).

reversal.statement: It is turned back on or off, where it is not enforced. Where it is, only the Super Admin's enforcement decides (BR-1, BR-2).

planningRules.rule: Confirm the person before resetting. This clears somebody's second factor, and the wrong name locks one person out and strips another's protection in the same act (BR-6).
Never write the reason. It is the record of how this person's identity was confirmed before their protection was cleared, and "lost phone" is not that (BR-6, E7).

planningRules.rule: Never return anything about a password beyond whether one has been set. No password, no temporary password and no one-time code is readable by anybody, in any report, at any time (BR-7, E9).

Name the accounts still on a temporary password, with how long. Each is a live credential sitting in an inbox, nothing expires it, and an account months old and never used is one somebody else may have opened the message for (BR-3, OQ-4).

Name the accounts whose record carries no contact. Nothing was ever sent to them, so nobody has ever signed in — and how a temporary password reaches a young student with no email of their own is raised in the specification and left open (E2, OQ-1).

Say that every account has a source. A student's and a guardian's come from an admission and an employee's from a staff record; there is no screen anywhere for creating one by hand, so an account with no source cannot exist (BR-1, E1).
Name disabled accounts that still hold a branch assignment. Disabling and withdrawing are separate acts, and a person can easily be left with one and not the other (BR-8).

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

steps.note: One step. The permission is granted to a named person and to nobody else (BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A grant by anybody other than the Super Admin is refused outright (E8).
plan.atomicity: One write. **The reader is branch-scoped**: a School Admin or Principal granted this sees only their own branch's entries, because branches are sealed, and only the Super Admin reads across them (BR-12, E2).

operations.name: audit.access.grant
operations.idempotencyKey: user_id, since a person holds one audit access grant
operations.purpose: Grant a named School Admin or Principal permission to read the audit trail.

parameters.name: user_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No School Admin or Principal matches. The permission is only for those two roles (BR-4).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their roles and the branch each is assigned to — the branch decides what they will be able to see (BR-12).

parameters.notes: The named School Admin or Principal. Nobody holds this by default (BR-4).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Who can now read the trail, and how much of it.

fields.name: grant_id
fields.description: The grant.

fields.name: granted_to
fields.description: The named person and their role (BR-4).

fields.name: sees
fields.description: Their own branch's entries only. Branches are sealed and only the Super Admin reads across them (BR-12, E2).

fields.name: includes_entries_about_themselves
fields.description: True. Whether a granted reader should see entries about their own actions is an open question this use case raises and does not answer — it means somebody can watch their own trail (OQ-3).

fields.name: reading_is_recorded
fields.description: True. Reading the trail is itself written to the trail, so somebody looking through it is as traceable as somebody acting (BR-11).

fields.name: holders_now
fields.description: How many people can read the trail in total. It is a permission in its own right and the number should be small (BR-4).

errors.meaning: Somebody other than the Super Admin attempted the grant.
errors.note: Only the Super Admin can grant access to the audit trail (BR-4).

planningRules.rule: Say what they will actually see. A granted reader sees their own branch's entries and nothing of any other, because branches are sealed — only the Super Admin reads across them (BR-12, E2).
Say that they will see entries about themselves. Somebody granted this can watch their own trail, and whether they should be able to is raised in the specification and left open (OQ-3).

Say that reading is recorded. Every look at the trail is written to the trail, so the person granted this is as traceable as anybody acting — which is worth saying to them, not just about them (BR-11).
Say how many people hold it. It is a permission in its own right precisely because the trail is what everything else is checked against, and nobody holds it by default (BR-4).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: The use case describes granting audit access and describes no revoking of it — no flow, no screen action and no rule covers taking it back. A grant made in error has no documented way back (BR-4).

request.text: Johar Town ke School Admin ko audit trail dekhne ki ijazat de dein
request.gloss: give the Johar Town School Admin permission to see the audit trail

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, nobody currently holding audit access.

steps.note: One named person (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Granted. They see Johar Town's entries and nothing of any other campus. Two things to tell them and one to note: every time they open the trail, that is itself written to it; they will see entries about their own actions, which the specification raises as a question and does not settle; and this is the only person besides the Super Admin who can read it at all — the use case describes granting this and describes no way to take it back.

steps.note: One read, and it is written to the trail as it runs (BR-11).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A search matching more entries than can be shown is paged and narrower filters are suggested, rather than the answer being truncated silently (E7).
plan.atomicity: A read that **writes**. Reading the trail is itself written to the trail, so the person searching is as traceable as the people they are searching (BR-11). Nothing in the trail can be edited or deleted by anybody (BR-2).

operations.name: audit.trail.read
operations.purpose: Search the audit trail by user, date, module, action or record.

parameters.name: user_phrase

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No user matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their roles.

parameters.notes: Where the question is about one person's actions.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.notes: The start of the period. **How far back the trail reaches is not specified anywhere** — the retention policy the rule refers to is defined nowhere (BR-7, OQ-1).

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.notes: The end of it.

parameters.name: module
parameters.notes: Which part of the system (BR-3).

parameters.name: action
parameters.notes: What kind of action. **Nothing is exempt** — creating, changing, deleting, approving, signing in, and every override recorded elsewhere in the system (BR-1).

parameters.name: record_phrase

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No record matches, or it is outside the actor's branch (BR-12).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the records that match with their type.

parameters.notes: Where the question is about one record — a student, a result, an invoice.

parameters.name: overrides_only
parameters.notes: Only the overrides recorded elsewhere in the system. These are the entries an investigation usually starts from (BR-1, BR-9).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What was done, when, by whom, and to what.

fields.name: entries
fields.description: When, user, **the role they held at the time**, the branch they were acting in, module, action, record, before and after, and any reason given (BR-1, BR-8, BR-9, BR-10).

fields.name: role_at_the_time
fields.description: The role the user held when they acted, which may since have changed. Reading their current role instead would explain nothing (BR-8).

fields.name: before_and_after
fields.description: What the value was and what it became. A change entry explains the change rather than merely noting one (BR-10).

fields.name: reasons
fields.description: The reason given where the action required one. An approval or an override with no reason recorded is an action nobody can question (BR-9).

fields.name: overrides
fields.description: Overrides recorded elsewhere in the system, gathered here (BR-1).

fields.name: scope
fields.description: The actor's own branch, or every branch for the Super Admin (BR-12, E2).

fields.name: total_matching
fields.description: How many entries match. Where it is more than can be shown, the search is paged and narrower filters are suggested rather than truncated silently (E7).

fields.name: earliest_available
fields.description: How far back the trail reaches. **The retention policy is defined nowhere**, so this is the practical limit on any investigation (BR-7, OQ-1).

fields.name: reads_not_recorded
fields.description: Reading the trail is recorded; reading an ordinary record generally is not — whether a salary or a safeguarding note should be, is unanswered (BR-11, OQ-5).

errors.meaning: The acting user does not hold the audit permission.
errors.note: Reading the trail is a permission in its own right and nobody holds it by default (BR-4).

errors.meaning: A branch-scoped reader searched another branch's entries.
errors.note: Branches are sealed and only the Super Admin reads across them (BR-12).

errors.meaning: More entries match than can be shown.
errors.note: Narrower filters are suggested — a date range or a module (BR-3).

operations.writesOnRead: An audit entry naming the actor, the search and the time. **Reading the trail is itself written to the trail**, so somebody looking through it is as traceable as somebody acting (BR-11). A search whose result is never shown has still recorded the looking.

planningRules.rule: Say that the search itself is recorded. Reading the trail is written to the trail, and the person asking is entitled to know that before they ask rather than to discover it in it (BR-11).

Give the role the user held **at the time**, not the one they hold now. Somebody who approved a result as a coordinator and is now a teacher is explained by the first and confused by the second (BR-8).
Give before and after, not just that something changed. A change entry exists to explain the change, and "marks lock changed" answers nothing (BR-10).
Give the reason where the action carried one. An approval or an override with no reason recorded is an action nobody can question, and the reason is the whole of what an investigation reads (BR-9).
Never claim how far back the trail goes. The retention policy the rule refers to is defined nowhere, and it is the practical limit on every investigation (BR-7, OQ-1).

Say what the trail does not record. Reading the trail is recorded; reading an ordinary record — a salary, a safeguarding note — generally is not, so an investigation into who **looked** at something will usually find nothing (BR-11, OQ-5).
Never narrow a search to make it fit. Where too many entries match, page it and say so — a silently truncated trail is worse than a slow one (E7).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing in the trail and cannot be taken out of it — the entry recording the search is written like any other and is as uneditable as the rest (BR-2, BR-11).

request.text: is salary ka record kis kis ne dekha hai?
request.gloss: who has looked at this salary record?

resolvedPlans.context: Principal with audit access.

steps.note: The search runs and will find changes, not viewings (PR-6).

resolvedPlans.outcome: This will show who **changed** the record and not who looked at it. Reading the trail is recorded; reading an ordinary record generally is not, and whether a salary or a safeguarding note should be an exception is raised in the specification and left open. So an answer of "nobody" here means nobody changed it, not that nobody saw it.

steps.note: One step. The class is created for the academic session the controller holds — the session is never taken from the request (BR-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Name uniqueness, the subject requirement, the acting role and whether a session is open at all are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the class, its attached subjects and the audit entry together or not at all. It creates no sections and no students (BR-10) — it is a structure that other things key off. Once created, the class becomes readable by attendance, timetable, assignment and examination in the same request (BR-8).

operations.name: class.create
operations.idempotencyKey: class_name + session_id + branch_id, which is the same triple BR-3 uses to decide a class already exists
operations.purpose: Create a class for the open academic session with its type and the subjects it carries.

parameters.name: class_name
parameters.notes: 2 to 60 characters, unique within the academic session and branch (BR-3). Passed exactly as the school says it — Grade 4, Class IV, Prep are different names and the school's own is the one that appears on every register.

parameters.name: class_order
parameters.notes: Where the class sits in the school's sequence, so lists and promotion read in the right order. Only where the request states it; never inferred from the name, because Prep, Nursery and Grade 1 do not sort themselves.

parameters.name: class_type
parameters.notes: Fixed means every student takes the same subjects; Subject Wise means students take a selection, which changes how fees, timetables and results are calculated (BR-4). It cannot be changed once students are placed (BR-6), so it is never guessed.

parameters.name: subject_ids

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. A subject named here does not exist. Creating it is a separate act on the subject list.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates.

parameters.notes: At least one is required — a class with no subjects cannot be timetabled, taught or examined (BR-5, E2).

parameters.name: compulsory_subject_ids
parameters.notes: Only meaningful for a Subject Wise class, where an optional subject is one a student may choose not to take. Omitted for a Fixed class, where every student takes everything.

parameters.name: age_range
parameters.notes: The ages the class normally takes, used to check an inquiry at the point it is submitted (UC-02-01 BR-3). Only where the request states it.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: class_id
fields.description: The class.

fields.name: class_name
fields.description: As given.

fields.name: class_order
fields.description: Its place in the sequence.

fields.name: class_type
fields.description: Fixed or Subject Wise.

fields.name: subjects
fields.description: Those attached, with whether each is compulsory.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: The academic session it belongs to, and cannot leave (BR-2).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Active.

fields.name: published_to
fields.description: The modules that can now read it — attendance, timetable, assignment, examination (BR-8).

errors.meaning: A class of that name already exists in this session and branch.
errors.note: Message names the session. Two classes called Grade 4 in one session make every list ambiguous (BR-3).

errors.meaning: No subject was attached.
errors.note: Message: "Attach at least one subject. A class with no subjects cannot be timetabled, taught or examined."

errors.meaning: No academic session is open.
errors.note: A class belongs to a session, so there is nothing to create it in.

errors.meaning: A Coordinator attempted to create a class.
errors.note: Only a School Admin creates classes; Coordinators create the sections under them. In practice the capability is absent from a Coordinator's allow-list.

planningRules.rule: Never guess the class type. Fixed and Subject Wise change how fees, timetables and results are calculated (BR-4), and the type cannot be changed once a single student is placed (BR-6) — so a wrong guess is locked in for a whole session.
Never infer class_order from the name. Prep, Nursery, KG and Grade 1 do not sort themselves, and the order is what lists and promotion read.
Pass the class name exactly as the school says it. It appears on every register, invoice and result sheet, and the school's own wording — Grade 4, Class IV, Prep — is the one they will look for.

Never create a class to get past a refusal somewhere else. A section that cannot be created, an import row naming a class that does not exist, or a placement with nowhere to go are all statements about the structure — and creating the missing class silently invents part of the school's shape.
session_id and branch_id come from $session. A class for next year is created in next year's session, which the actor opens first; a plan never takes the session from the request (BR-2).
Never plan a class creation for a set. Each carries a type, an order and a subject list that someone decided; a batch decides none of them.

reversal.statement: There is no delete. A class no longer run is deactivated through class.deactivate, and even that is refused while it holds an active section or a placed student (BR-9). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

parameters.name: class_id

planningRules.rule: Send only what the request changes. Every field sent is a recorded change that propagates to attendance, timetable and examination in the same request (BR-8); resupplying an unchanged name records an edit nobody made and reprints registers for nothing.
Never send class_type unless the request changes it. It is refused once students are placed (E3), so including it in an unrelated edit turns a rename into a refusal and neither happens.

Add and remove subjects by explicit list, never by replacing the set. A replacement built from what the actor mentioned drops every subject they did not name, and E4 would only catch the ones already carrying work.

Never treat SUBJECT_IN_USE as an obstacle. Marks, a timetable slot or an assignment already exist against that subject this session, and removing it would orphan them — the answer is that the subject stays until the session ends.
Never rename a class to resolve a duplicate. E1 means two classes share a name in one session, and which one should change is the school's decision, not a tidy-up.
branch_id comes from $session, and the class is resolved within the open academic session. A class in a past session is not edited from this one (BR-2).

reversal.statement: There is no undo. A wrong change is changed again, and both stay in the audit log with their previous values. The propagation to registers, timetables and result sheets has already happened either way (BR-8). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

planningRules.rule: Report who a set resolves to, by name, before the plan is emitted. Placement puts children on registers, starts their attendance, makes them billable and sends their guardians into a WhatsApp group — none of which is undone by a later move.
Send section_id and never class_id. The section determines its class, and sending both invites them to disagree — a student on one class's register and another's section.

Never choose the section. Where the request names none, ask; where the named one is full, E1 and E7 say so and the alternatives come back for a person to pick from. Which room a child sits in is not a planner's decision.

Never substitute the placement date. Attendance is markable from it (BR-6), so a date invented here decides whether a child was absent for a month. E2 and E3 refusing one are the system asking a person to say when the child actually started.

Never treat ALREADY_PLACED as a reason to place again. A student holds one active placement per session (BR-12); moving them is a different capability that closes the old enrolment and needs a reason (BR-7).

planningRules.rule: Only the desk logs a visitor in. A request from somebody saying they are the visitor, or asking to log themselves in, has no route — the visitor is not an actor (BR-1, E10).

Never clear a possible match. It is shown to the desk rather than resolved, because a name is not an identity and only the desk can ask (BR-11). Set possible_match_cleared only from the desk's own statement after the match has been put to them — never on a first attempt, and never because the visitor insists.

Never retry a barred visitor — not with another spelling, another number, or the cleared flag. The system stopping them is the whole point of the blocklist: the person on duty should not be the only thing between a barred person and the school (BR-3, E4).
Report an unchecked visitor as unchecked. Where no blocklist is configured the check returns nothing, and a visitor logged in on those terms must never be described as cleared (E5, AC-10).
Never choose the pass. It is the one physically handed over, and the log-out accounts for that pass and no other (BR-5, BR-9).

Log in from the pre-registration where there is one. An expected visitor and an unexpected one are not handled identically — the desk confirms details already there rather than taking them again (BR-2, A1).
A prospective family enquiring is still a visitor here. Log the visit; the inquiry is recorded separately, in admissions (BR-10, A5).

reversal.statement: No capability undoes a visit. It is closed when the visitor leaves — visit.log.out, UC-29-02 — which records a departure, not a mistake. A visit is never deleted (BR-8, E9).

planningRules.rule: Never name the missing items yourself. Return to Staff and Contact family both refuse without them (E2), and a list a planner composed describes what it thinks is absent rather than what the reviewer decided is absent.

Never change the outcome to get past a refusal. A forward refused for an incomplete field is not a return; it is an incomplete inquiry, and forwarding it as something else moves it while leaving the gap.
Never re-emit the review after ALREADY_FORWARDED. A second review is not recorded and the inquiry has moved on; the answer is where it is now.

Never chain an approval onto a forward. Review decides only whether the Principal should be asked (BR-9), and the Principal's decision is a separate capability with a separate allow-list entry.
Carry the actor's own words into review_note and missing_items. The Principal and the Staff member read them, and a planner's paraphrase loses what the reviewer actually noticed.

reversal.statement: There is no un-review. A review is a record of a check that happened, and it is recorded even when nothing changed (BR-1). Never reject an inquiry the school has not decided on. An incomplete one is returned (UC-02-02), a family who withdrew is closed (UC-02-11); rejecting either tells a family no on the school's behalf when no decision was taken.
Never plan a rejection for a set. Each one is a decision on a child and a message to a family, and neither can be recalled.
Report the decision and the send separately. The rejection stands even where the message failed (E4), and a family who has not been told is a fact worth stating.

reversal.statement: There is no un-reject, and the enquiry it closes cannot be re-opened either (UC-02-11 E8). A decision is never edited; where the school changes its mind, that is a fresh inquiry, not a reversal. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

planningRules.rule: Never record a score without attendance, and never send 0 for an absent applicant. Zero means they sat the test and scored nothing; absent means they did not sit it. The two look alike in a sentence and mean opposite things to the decision (BR-2, BR-4).

Never guess which applicant. A score against the wrong temporary ID is the failure BR-1 exists to prevent, and it surfaces weeks later as an admission decision taken on somebody else's paper. Where two applicants could match the name, ask.

Pass the score exactly as given. Never clamp it to the maximum, never round it, never convert a percentage into a mark. E1 refusing a score above the maximum means the paper and the configuration disagree, and that is worth someone looking at.
Never change attendance to make a score save. E3 says the applicant is recorded absent; marking them present so a number fits rewrites whether a child turned up.

Never judge the score. No pass mark is applied here, no eligibility is set and nobody is admitted (BR-5). Reporting a score as good, poor or a pass reads a judgement into a number that the school has not made yet.
Keep marker_remark out of anything the family sees. It is internal by rule (BR-8), and a reply that quotes it back into a message to a parent breaks that quietly.

Never reschedule to deal with an absence in the same breath. Missing a test is not a result (BR-10); recording the absence and deciding whether to offer another date are separate acts by separate judgements.

reversal.statement: A recorded result is not deleted or overwritten. planningRules.rule: Never compose the correction reason. An admission decision may already have been taken on the value being replaced (BR-7), and the reason is what someone reads when they go back to find out how that happened.

Correct only what the request says is wrong. Resupplying the existing attendance alongside a score change records a correction to something nobody corrected, and the audit trail then shows two changes where one happened.

Never correct attendance in order to get a score in. Where the request says the applicant did attend, correcting both together is right; where it only supplies a number, E3 refusing it means the record says they were absent, and that is a fact to check rather than an obstacle.

Report decision_already_taken whenever it comes back true. A decision made on a score that has since changed is the single most consequential thing this capability can surface, and it goes nowhere unless it is said.
Never chain a re-decision onto a correction. A decision is never edited (UC-02-07 BR-11); where the corrected score changes what should have happened, that is a further decision someone takes.

reversal.statement: A correction is itself the correction mechanism, and it is not reversed — a further correction is another recorded change with its own reason. The previous values all stay in the audit trail, so the sequence of what was recorded and when survives. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

errors.meaning: The applicant has already been admitted or rejected.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the eligibility reason. The Principal reads it before deciding a child's admission, and BR-3 requires it either way precisely so the judgement can be defended later. A planner's reason is a judgement nobody made.

Never infer eligibility from the score. No pass mark exists (UC-02-06 BR-5), the form matters as much as the number (BR-1), and an absence is shown to the decider rather than treated as a result (BR-12). The flag is a person's judgement on both together.

Never chain an admission onto a flag. Eligibility and approval are separate acts by separate people (BR-2), and one plan doing both erases the check the separation exists to provide.

reversal.statement: A flag is a recorded judgement and is not withdrawn. A change of view is a further flag with its own reason, and both stay readable. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

steps.note: One step, whether the request names one applicant or several. Everything downstream — student, guardian, family, enrolment, accounts, credentials — is created inside it (BR-5, BR-6, BR-7). There is no sequence to plan and nothing to wire between steps.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Eligibility, section capacity, the numbering pattern and whether the applicant has already been decided are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors; the plan does not test for them beforehand. A failed credentials message does not fail the admission (E8) — the student exists and the family has not been told, which is an outcome to report.
plan.atomicity: Each admission is atomic in itself: the student, guardian, family, enrolment and accounts are created together or not at all, so a failure part way leaves nothing behind (E7). Across a batch the guarantee is different — each applicant is approved individually inside it and one failure does not abandon the rest (BR-10), so a partial result is the normal shape. The credentials message is separate again and does not block. Report all three layers: who was admitted, who was not and why, and who has not yet been told.

errors.meaning: A School Admin attempted to approve an admission.
errors.note: Only the Principal decides (BR-2). In practice the capability is absent from a School Admin allow-list.

errors.meaning: The applicant has not been flagged eligible.
errors.note: Message: "This applicant has not been flagged eligible yet." Flagging is the School Admin's act, and chaining it here would erase the separation in BR-2.

errors.meaning: The chosen section is full.
errors.note: Message names the section. Choosing another is the Principal's decision, and approving without a section is also open to them (BR-8).

errors.meaning: No student numbering pattern is configured.
errors.note: No student ID or roll number can be generated (BR-6). This is configuration, not a decision problem.

errors.meaning: Record creation failed part way.
errors.note: Message: "The admission could not be completed. Nothing has been created." The write is atomic, so there is no half-made student to clean up and no compensating call to make.

errors.meaning: The credentials message failed to send.
errors.written: The student, guardian, family, enrolment and accounts all exist.
errors.notWritten: The family does not have the credentials.
errors.note: Not a failure of the admission. Report both halves — a family without credentials cannot sign in, and the student is already on the register.

errors.meaning: The applicant has already been admitted or rejected.
errors.note: The message names the date. Open the student record instead.

planningRules.rule: Report who a set resolves to, by name, before the plan is emitted. This creates student records, roll numbers, guardian logins and fee liability, and none of it can be uncreated. "In sab ko admit kar do" is a phrase with no number in it; the names are what the Principal is actually approving.

Never chain an eligibility flag onto an admission. E3 refusing an unflagged applicant is BR-2 working — two people, deliberately — and flagging them here to make the admission succeed removes the only check standing before a child's record is created.

Send section_id and never class_id. The section determines its class, and the backend derives it; sending both invites them to disagree and puts a student in one class's register and another's section.

Never choose a section. Where the request names none, omit it — the Principal may approve and place the student later (BR-8). Where the named one is full, E5 says so, and picking another puts a child in a class on a planner's judgement.
Never re-emit with a different section after SECTION_AT_CAPACITY. The section was the Principal's choice, and the alternatives come back for a person to pick from.

Report the three layers separately: who was admitted, who failed and why, and whose credentials have not gone out. A batch reported as a single success hides both the failures BR-10 insists on listing and the families who cannot sign in (E8).
Never re-emit after ALREADY_DECIDED, and never treat it as a reason to correct anything. A decision is never edited; a correction is a further recorded decision (BR-11), which is not this capability.

Never chain anything onto an admission. The credentials, the fee liability, the register entry and the portal access all follow from it automatically; adding a message or an enrolment step duplicates a record that already exists.

reversal.statement: There is none, and this is the most consequential place in the module where that is true. Admission creates a student ID and a roll number that are never reused (BR-6), a guardian login, a family code, an enrolment and fee liability. A decision is never edited (BR-11) — a correction is a further recorded decision, and undoing an admission means deactivating a student record, which is UC-03-01's business and refused outright once a fee transaction references it. The controller must not attempt a compensating call under any circumstances.

steps.note: One step. The reason is mandatory because the family is told it (BR-4), and it is carried onto the closure of their enquiry so a second reason is never invented for it.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the applicant has already been decided, and the acting role, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors. A failed message does not fail the rejection.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the decision, the applicant's status, the closure of the enquiry and the audit entry together or not at all. No student record is created. The rejection message is separate and does not block — so the ordinary partial outcome is a rejection that stands with a family who has not been told. The enquiry closes carrying the rejection reason and cannot afterwards be re-opened (UC-02-11 E8).

parameters.name: applicant_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No applicant matches in this branch at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with temporary ID, child name, target class and test score. Never pick the likeliest — this decision creates a person's record.

parameters.notes: The applicant, resolved from how the actor named them — the temporary ID, or the child's name. Everything from the form to the decision hangs off this identifier.

parameters.name: rejection_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Mandatory — the family is told why, so an unexplained rejection is not permitted (BR-4, E4). The Principal's own words, carried across untranslated.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

errors.meaning: Reject was chosen with no reason.

errors.meaning: A School Admin attempted to decide.
errors.note: Only the Principal decides (BR-2).

errors.meaning: The applicant has already been decided.
The rejection message failed to send.

errors.notWritten: The family has not been told.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the rejection reason. It is sent to a family in the school's name and carried onto the closure of their enquiry, where it is read in the loss report afterwards. E4 refuses the rejection without one precisely so a person writes it.
Never re-emit after ALREADY_DECIDED, and never treat it as a correction. A decision is never edited (BR-11); the answer is what was decided and when.
Never plan a rejection for a set. Each is a decision on a child and a message to a family, and neither can be recalled. Where several are to be rejected they are several plans, each reported.
Never soften or rewrite the reason. It is carried onto the closure and read later, and the words the Principal chose are the record.
Report the decision and the send separately. The rejection stands even where the message failed (E8), and a family who has not been told is a fact worth stating.

reversal.statement: There is no un-reject, and the enquiry it closes cannot be re-opened (UC-02-11 E8). A decision is never edited (BR-11); where the school changes its mind, that is a fresh inquiry and a fresh applicant, not a reversal. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the matched record is currently enrolled, whether it transferred to another branch, and whether the details differ from the inquiry, are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.

operations.name: readmission.match.confirm
operations.idempotencyKey: inquiry_id + student_id, so a repeat does not record a second confirmation
operations.purpose: Link a re-admission inquiry to the existing student record it belongs to, so the school reuses that record rather than creating a second.

parameters.name: inquiry_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No re-admission inquiry matches in this branch.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with child name, previous student ID and year last attended.

parameters.notes: The re-admission inquiry, resolved from how the actor named it — a reference, the child's name, or the previous student ID.

parameters.name: student_id
parameters.notes: The former student record being confirmed. Passed exactly as given — a system-issued identifier is never re-spelled or transliterated (request-language). Where the request names a person rather than an ID, ask for the ID: this is the field that decides whether a second record gets created.

parameters.name: confirmation_note
parameters.notes: Maximum 250 characters. Where the details differ from the record and the admin is confirming anyway, what they checked.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The link, and what the record holds.

fields.name: inquiry_id
fields.description: The inquiry, now marked a confirmed re-admission.

fields.name: student_id
fields.description: The record it is linked to.

fields.name: student_name
fields.description: The name on the record, for reading back against the inquiry.

fields.name: student_status
fields.description: Left, Struck off or Transferred.

fields.name: year_last_attended
fields.description: From the record, not from what the family said.

fields.name: class_last_attended
fields.description: Used to default the return class later (BR-6).

fields.name: outstanding_balance
fields.description: Carried from the previous enrolment. Shown to the Principal before the decision, because it bears on whether the school wants the family back (BR-8).

fields.name: detail_mismatch
fields.description: Where the name or date of birth on the record differs from the inquiry (E3). Reported, not hidden.

errors.meaning: The previous student ID matches no record.
errors.note: The inquiry continues as an ordinary new admission and the admission form is sent as usual (BR-12). That is a different path, not a retry.

errors.meaning: The matched record is currently enrolled.
errors.note: The message names the class. A currently enrolled child is not a re-admission, and this is usually a mistyped ID.

errors.meaning: The name or date of birth on the record differs from the inquiry.
errors.note: The message names the record. Resolving it is the reviewer's work at review, not later (BR-3).

errors.meaning: A Staff user attempted to confirm.
errors.note: Only a School Admin may confirm a re-admission match. In practice the capability is absent from a Staff allow-list.

errors.meaning: The matched student transferred to another branch.
errors.note: Message names the branch. Inter-branch student transfer is UC-23-04 and a different use case entirely (BR-10).

planningRules.rule: Never confirm a match the request has not stated. The system's proposal is a proposal, not a fact (BR-2), and confirming is a person saying it is the right child. A planner confirming on the strength of a name match is exactly how one child ends up with two records — the failure this whole use case exists to prevent (BR-1).
Never re-spell or reconstruct the previous student ID. It is what the family quoted from a document, and a corrected version points at a different child or at nobody.

Never treat NO_MATCH as a retry. Where the ID matches nothing and the family cannot supply a correct one, the inquiry continues as an ordinary new admission with the admission form sent as usual (BR-12). That is a different path someone chooses, not a fallback the controller takes.

Report detail_mismatch and outstanding_balance whenever they come back. The balance bears on whether the school wants the family back (BR-8) and the Principal is meant to see it before deciding; a mismatch in name or date of birth is the reviewer's to resolve now rather than later (BR-3).
Never chain a forward or an approval onto a confirmation. Confirming the match is one act; whether the school takes the family back is a separate decision by different people.

reversal.statement: There is no unconfirm written. A confirmation links an inquiry to a record and changes nothing on the record itself, so the consequence is contained — but correcting a wrong link is not specified, and a re-admission confirmed against the wrong child would carry that child's history forward. See the open question.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Section capacity, the confirmed match and whether the section filled while the decision was pending are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors; the plan does not test for them beforehand.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the reactivation, the closure of the previous enrolment, the new enrolment and the audit entry together or not at all — a failure part way leaves the record unchanged (E7). The student keeps their original student ID and roll number (BR-5), so nothing new is issued and there is no second record to reconcile. The previous enrolment is closed rather than deleted, and its attendance, marks and fee history stay attached (BR-7).
