errors.meaning: The re-admission match has not been confirmed by a School Admin.
errors.note: Nothing proceeds as a re-admission until the match is confirmed (BR-3). Confirming it here would remove that check.

errors.meaning: The return section is full.
errors.note: Message names the section. Choosing another is the Principal's decision, and approving without one is open to them.

errors.meaning: The section filled while the decision was awaiting approval.
errors.note: The same outcome as E5 with a different history behind it. Report which, because the Principal chose that section when it had room.

errors.meaning: Reactivation failed part way.
errors.notWritten: No enrolment created, the previous one still open.
errors.note: Message: "The re-admission could not be completed. The record is unchanged." Atomic, so there is nothing to clean up and no compensating call.

errors.meaning: The student transferred to another branch.
errors.note: Inter-branch student transfer is UC-23-04 (BR-10).

planningRules.rule: Never chain a match confirmation onto a reactivation. E4 refusing an unconfirmed match is BR-3 working — a person has to say this is the right child before their history is carried forward — and confirming it here to make the reactivation succeed removes the only check standing before that.

Never choose the return section. The class above the one they left is a suggestion and never applied silently (BR-6); where the request names none, omit it and the Principal places them later. Where the named one is full, E5 says so.
Distinguish E5 from E6 when reporting. Both say the section is full, but E6 means it filled while the Principal was deciding — they chose it when it had room, and that is a different conversation.
Never supply updated_guardian_contact speculatively. It changes the guardian's sign-in contact (BR-9), so a number picked up in passing locks a family out of the portal.

Never plan applicant.admit for a returning student. That creates a new student record with a new ID, which is the exact failure this use case exists to prevent (BR-1) — and the two records would then split one child's attendance, marks and fee history between them.

Report the carried balance and the gap. The balance bears on the decision (BR-8) and the gap is deliberately preserved (BR-11); a reply that presents the re-admission as a clean continuous enrolment misstates the record.

reversal.statement: There is none. Reactivation closes the previous enrolment and opens a new one against a record that is now Enrolled, billable and on the class register. Reversing it means marking the student left again, which is UC-03-01's business and a different act with its own reasons. The controller must not attempt a compensating call — and must never fall back to applicant.admit, which would create the second record the whole use case exists to prevent.

returns.description: The enquiry as opened, with the reference to quote back to the family.

fields.name: inquiry_id
fields.description: The enquiry's id.

fields.name: reference
fields.description: Gapless per branch and academic session, quotable to the family.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Pending review on creation.

fields.name: follow_up_date
fields.description: The date set, whether given or supplied by the API (BR-3).

fields.name: owner_name
fields.description: Who is responsible for the follow-up.

fields.name: existing
fields.description: True where an open enquiry already existed for this child and number and was returned instead of a second being created (BR-7).

errors.meaning: The contact number is missing or malformed.
errors.note: Message: "Enter a valid contact number. An enquiry cannot be followed up without one."

errors.meaning: No enquiry source was given.
The follow-up date given is before today.
errors.note: Do not retry with today's date substituted. The date came from the request and correcting it is the actor's decision.

errors.meaning: The target class does not exist in the current academic session.
An open enquiry already holds this child name and contact number for this academic session.
errors.written: Nothing new. The existing enquiry is returned with existing true.
errors.note: Not a failure — BR-7 says the second attempt opens the first. Report the existing reference rather than announcing a new enquiry. UC-02-10 defines no E-id for it because on screen the existing enquiry simply opens; see the open question.

planningRules.rule: Never fabricate a contact number, and never proceed without one. It is the single mandatory field that makes an enquiry an enquiry (BR-1), and an enquiry recorded against a guessed number is a lead nobody can follow up.

Never set enquiry_source to Online form. That value is stamped by the family's own submission (BR-2) and setting it by hand records a lie about where the family came from, which is what the school's advertising decisions are made on.

Never set follow_up_date to today to get past a refusal, and never invent one to fill the field. Omitting it is correct and the API supplies one (BR-3); substituting one takes a decision that belongs to the person who will do the following up.

Pass the child's and guardian's names exactly as the request gave them. A name recorded here is what the family will be greeted by on the phone, and it is matched against later when the same family enquires again (BR-7).

Never re-emit the write with the failing field removed. A refused mobile number, a missing source or a class outside the session are all the API stating something about the enquiry, and an enquiry saved without them is worse than none.
Never chain a message onto this plan. Recording an enquiry sends the family nothing; telling them anything is inquiry.message, planned separately and logged as a contact.

reversal.statement: There is no delete. An enquiry recorded in error is closed as not interested through inquiry.close, which keeps it and its history (BR-8, and UC-02-11 BR-4). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, with an open enquiry already held for that child and number.

steps.note: The plan is unchanged. The API recognises the open enquiry from the same child name and number and returns it (BR-7); the plan neither checked for it nor branched.

steps.note: One step. The enquiry is resolved from how the actor named it; the channel, the outcome and the next date all come from what they said happened.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the enquiry is still open, and whether the date is valid, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write. The contact log entry, the incremented attempt count, the moved follow-up date and the audit entry are written together or not at all. Earlier notes are appended to, never replaced (BR-5), so nothing already recorded can be lost by this call.

operations.name: inquiry.contact.log
operations.idempotencyKey: inquiry_id + channel + outcome + the contact timestamp, so a repeated call does not inflate the attempt count that BR-6 relies on
operations.purpose: Record a contact attempt against an enquiry with its outcome, and set the next follow-up date.

parameters.name: inquiry_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No open enquiry matches, or none in this branch. Neither is reached by guessing a reference.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with child name, guardian and target class. Two families of the same name is the ordinary case here, not the exception.

parameters.notes: The enquiry, resolved from how the actor named it — a reference, the child's name, or the guardian's number. Never a reference the planner composed.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.type: enum: Phone | WhatsApp | Email | In person
parameters.notes: How the contact was made. Required with the outcome (BR-4).

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.type: enum: Reached | No answer | Wrong number | Call back later | Not interested
parameters.notes: What happened. Mandatory — recording a contact with no outcome tells the next caller nothing (BR-4).

parameters.name: next_follow_up_date
parameters.notes: Not in the past. Mandatory: a contact recorded without a next date is refused, because the lead then disappears (BR-4, E4).

parameters.name: note
parameters.notes: What the family said, in their words. Appended with author and timestamp (BR-5).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The contact as logged, and where the enquiry now stands.

fields.name: contact_id
fields.description: The log entry.

fields.name: attempts
fields.description: The attempt count after this one. Drives the stale rule (BR-6).

fields.name: status
fields.description: The enquiry's status, which may have moved to Contacted or to Stale.

fields.name: next_follow_up_date
fields.description: The date now set.

fields.name: became_stale
fields.description: True where this attempt took the enquiry past the configured limit and it dropped out of the daily list (BR-6).

errors.meaning: No next follow-up date was given.
errors.note: Message: "Set the next follow-up date before saving this contact." Ask for the date; do not supply one.

errors.meaning: No outcome was given.
The enquiry was closed as not interested.
errors.note: Message names the closure date. Re-opening is inquiry.reopen and is a separate decision, never chained onto this.

errors.meaning: The next follow-up date is before today.

planningRules.rule: Never log a contact for a message you also sent. inquiry.message counts as a contact attempt in its own right (UC-02-12 BR-7), and logging one alongside it makes the attempt count and the message log disagree, which is the exact thing BR-7 exists to prevent.

Read the outcome from what the request states, not from its tone. "Soch rahe hain" is Call back later; "fees zyada hai" is a note, not an outcome; "mana kar diya" is a closure and belongs to inquiry.close. Where the sentence does not settle which outcome it is, ask rather than choosing — the outcome is what the next caller reads before dialling.
Never supply next_follow_up_date yourself. The refusal in E4 is the system insisting that a person decide when to call back, and a date invented here is a commitment nobody made.

Never chain a re-open onto a contact logged against a closed enquiry. Re-opening is a judgement with its own reason and its own record (UC-02-11 BR-6), and doing it silently to make a log succeed hides that the enquiry was closed.
Put what the family said in note, not in outcome. The outcome is a fixed set the follow-up list is filtered on; the words are what the next person needs.

reversal.statement: A contact log is history and is never removed. A wrong entry is corrected by logging the truth after it, because BR-5 appends and never overwrites. The controller has no compensating call.

steps.note: One step. The reason is the point of the act — closing without one makes the loss report useless (BR-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the enquiry is already closed, and whether it has been taken forward to an admission, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write. The status change, the closure record, the contact-history entry and the audit entry are written together or not at all. Nothing is deleted — the enquiry and its full history stay readable on the Not Interested List (BR-4). Nothing is sent to the family (BR-11).

operations.name: inquiry.close
operations.idempotencyKey: inquiry_id, since an enquiry has one closure at a time and a repeat returns ALREADY_CLOSED rather than recording a second
operations.purpose: Close an enquiry as not interested, recording why, and remove it from the follow-up list and every reminder.

parameters.name: inquiry_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No enquiry matches in this branch.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with child name, guardian and status. Two families of the same name is ordinary here.

parameters.notes: The enquiry, resolved from how the actor named it — a reference, the child's name, or the guardian's number.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.type: enum: Fee too high | Chose another school | Moved away | Distance too far | No seat in the class wanted | Timing not suitable | No response after follow-up | Rejected at approval | Other
parameters.notes: Mandatory. A closure with no reason teaches the school nothing and makes the loss report useless (BR-2).

parameters.name: other_reason
parameters.notes: Required when reason is Other (BR-3, E2). Omit otherwise — sending it with a listed reason records a second explanation nobody asked for.

parameters.name: competitor_school
parameters.notes: Where the family named the school they chose. Only where the request states it; never inferred from the area.

parameters.name: closing_note
parameters.notes: Appended to the contact history, never replacing it. The family's words belong here.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The enquiry as closed, and what it kept.

fields.name: inquiry_id
fields.description: The enquiry closed.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Not interested.

fields.name: closed_on
fields.description: DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm, school-local.

fields.name: closed_by
fields.description: The acting user.

fields.name: previous_status
fields.description: What it was before closing. Restored by inquiry.reopen (BR-7).

fields.name: reopenable
fields.description: False where the closure followed a rejection at approval (UC-02-11 E8).

errors.meaning: No reason was given.
errors.note: Message: "Select a reason before closing this enquiry." Ask which reason; do not choose one.

errors.meaning: Reason is Other with no free text.
The enquiry was already closed.
errors.note: The message names the closure date. Not a failure to retry, and not a reason to re-open.

errors.meaning: The enquiry was taken forward to a completed admission.
errors.note: Message names the admission date. The family is a student (BR-10); there is nothing here to close.

planningRules.rule: Never close an enquiry the family has not refused. Closing removes it from every reminder (BR-1), and a family still considering who is closed is a family the school stops calling. "Soch rahe hain" and "baad mein batayenge" are contact outcomes, not closures.

Read the reason from what the family actually said, and never fall back on Other to get past a refusal. Other exists for reasons the list does not hold, and using it as a default makes the whole list stop meaning anything (BR-3). Where the sentence does not settle which reason it is, ask.
Put the family's own words in closing_note, not in reason. reason is the fixed set the loss report is built from; the words are what the next person reads when the family comes back.
Never chain a re-open onto a refusal. An enquiry already closed is an answer (E3), and re-opening to make a close succeed is nonsense — it would then be closed again with a second reason.
Never chain a message onto this plan. Closing tells the family nothing by itself (BR-11); where they are to be told, that is inquiry.message, planned separately and logged as a message.

reversal.statement: inquiry.reopen restores the enquiry to its previous status and requires a new follow-up date (BR-5, BR-7). This is the one genuinely reversible act in the module, and deliberately so: closure is a judgement made in a hurry at a desk. Re-opening is a fresh decision with its own reason, never a compensating call the controller makes on its own after a failure.

resolvedPlans.request: close this one, they've stopped answering after four attempts
resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, on an enquiry already flagged Stale.

steps.note: Stale and closed are different states: stale drops the enquiry out of the daily list but keeps it open (UC-02-10 BR-6). Closing it is a decision someone takes.

resolvedPlans.outcome: The enquiry closes under No response after follow-up and leaves the pipeline. It stays on the Not Interested List, so if the family returns next year they are recognised.

steps.note: One step. Both the reason and the new date are required: a lead back in the list with no date disappears again (BR-7), and a lead closed and re-opened repeatedly should be visible rather than silent (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the enquiry is closed at all, and whether it was closed by a rejection, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write. The restored status, the re-opening record, the new follow-up date and the audit entry are written together or not at all. The closure is not erased — it stays in the history, so a re-opened enquiry never looks as though it was never closed (BR-8).

operations.name: inquiry.reopen
operations.idempotencyKey: inquiry_id + the closure it is re-opening, so a repeat does not inflate reopen_count
operations.purpose: Restore a closed enquiry to its previous status with a new follow-up date, keeping the closure in its history.

parameters.name: inquiry_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No enquiry matches in this branch.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with child name, guardian and status. Two families of the same name is ordinary here.

parameters.notes: The enquiry, resolved from how the actor named it — a reference, the child's name, or the guardian's number.

parameters.name: reopen_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 250 characters. Mandatory, so a lead closed and re-opened repeatedly is visible rather than silent (BR-6).

parameters.name: new_follow_up_date
parameters.notes: Not in the past. Mandatory: an enquiry back in the list with no date disappears again (BR-7, E6).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: inquiry_id
fields.description: The enquiry re-opened.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The status it held before closure, restored (BR-7).

fields.name: new_follow_up_date
fields.description: The date now set.

fields.name: reopen_count
fields.description: How many times this enquiry has been closed and re-opened. Visible rather than silent (BR-6).

errors.meaning: No reason was given for re-opening.
No new follow-up date was given.
errors.note: Message: "Set a follow-up date so the enquiry does not disappear again." Ask for the date; do not supply one.

errors.meaning: The follow-up date is before today.
The enquiry was closed by a rejection at approval.
errors.note: A rejection is a decision, and decisions are never edited (UC-02-07 BR-11). There is no path from here that re-opens it.

errors.meaning: The enquiry is already open.
errors.note: Report that it is open and at what status. UC-02-11 defines no E-id for it because the re-open control is only offered on a closed enquiry; see the open question.

planningRules.rule: Never re-open an enquiry as a step towards something else. Re-opening is a decision with a reason that someone stands behind (BR-6), and doing it silently so a contact log or a message succeeds hides that the enquiry had been closed.
Never supply new_follow_up_date yourself. E6 refuses the re-opening without one precisely so that a person commits to a date, and a date invented here re-opens a lead nobody has agreed to chase.

Never treat CLOSED_BY_REJECTION as something to route around. An enquiry closed by a Principal's rejection has a decision behind it, and decisions are never edited (UC-02-07 BR-11). There is no other capability that achieves it either.
Carry the actor's own words into reopen_reason. "Family ne wapas call kiya" is the reason; a planner's tidy paraphrase loses who did what.

reversal.statement: inquiry.close closes it again, with a fresh reason. The pair is genuinely reversible in both directions, and the history keeps every closure and every re-opening (BR-8), so the sequence survives however many times it happens. The controller must not close an enquiry on its own to undo a re-opening it made.

steps.note: One step, whether the request names one family or forty. The merge fields are resolved by the API against each enquiry's own values (BR-6), and a per-recipient result comes back (BR-11).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Channel availability, balance, merge-field resolution and the authorisation threshold are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors; the plan does not test for them beforehand. A bulk send above the threshold is not refused — it is queued for School Admin authorisation (E4), which is an outcome to report rather than a failure.
plan.atomicity: One write per recipient, and the batch does not stop at the first bad one: valid recipients are sent and failures are listed with their reason (BR-11). So a partial result is the normal shape here, not an accident. Each send writes a message record, a contact-log entry against the enquiry and an audit entry, and counts as a contact attempt (BR-7). Delivery status starts at Queued and is never reported optimistically (BR-9) — a run that reports success has queued the message, not delivered it.

errors.meaning: The enquiry holds no contact number or email.
errors.note: Adding a contact is a correction to the enquiry, recorded as one (BR-2). Never substitute a number from elsewhere.

errors.meaning: A template field cannot be filled from this enquiry's values.
errors.note: The send is blocked rather than going out with a gap in it (BR-6). The message names the field. Never fill it in by hand.

errors.meaning: A bulk send was attempted with free text.
errors.note: Message: "Select a template. Your own message can only be sent to one enquiry at a time."

errors.meaning: The batch is above the threshold a Staff user may send unaided.
errors.written: The batch is queued and School Admin is notified.
errors.note: Not a failure. Report that it has gone for approval, and to whom. Never split the batch to get under the threshold.

errors.meaning: There is no balance or quota for the channel.
errors.note: Never fall back to the other channel to get the message out — the channel was chosen, and the enquiry may not hold a contact for the other.

errors.meaning: The provider cannot be reached.
errors.written: The messages are queued and will send when it is reachable.
errors.note: Report them as queued, never as sent (BR-9).

errors.meaning: The template belongs to a different channel.
The enquiry was closed as not interested.
errors.note: Re-opening is a separate decision (UC-02-11), never chained onto a send.

planningRules.rule: Report what a set resolves to before anything is sent, and never send to a set the actor has not seen. A message cannot be unsent, and "sab ko bhej do" is a phrase with no number in it — the count is what the actor is actually approving.
Never split a batch to get under the authorisation threshold. The threshold exists so a School Admin sees a large send before it goes (BR-8); splitting it defeats that while looking like a success.

Never switch channel because one has no balance or no contact. The channel was chosen, and the other may reach a different person or nobody at all — a family who gave a number and no email is not reachable by email (BR-3).

Never fill an unresolved merge field by hand. E2 blocks the send precisely so a template does not go out with a gap or a guess where the child's class should be. The missing value belongs on the enquiry.
Report a send as queued, never as delivered. Delivery status is what the provider says, and the school believing a family was told when they were not is the failure BR-9 exists to prevent.
Never log a contact alongside a message. The send counts as a contact attempt in its own right (BR-7), and logging one too makes the attempt count and the message log disagree.
Never use free text for more than one recipient. E3 refuses it, and the reason is that text sent to many can neither be reviewed before it goes nor reused after.
Send only to the contact on the enquiry. A number the actor supplies in passing is a correction to the enquiry first, recorded as one (BR-2), and never a destination for this send.

reversal.statement: A message cannot be unsent. The log entry, the attempt count and the delivery status are history. Where the wrong thing went out, the answer is another message, which is another planned send — never a compensating call the controller makes on its own.

planningRules.rule: Never write, soften or summarise the details. They are the parent's own words about their own child, and a complaint a planner drafted is a complaint nobody made (BR-3, E2).

Never choose the category — and never file words that describe harm under anything else. Where a parent's words describe a child being hurt, put "A child has been harmed" to them first. Filing it as staff conduct sends it into the ordinary queue, where the people it may concern can see it (BR-4, BR-9, E1).
Say where a harm allegation goes before it is raised. It goes to the Principal alone, bypassing the desk and the School Admin, and is readable only by those the Principal permits (BR-4, A1).

Say plainly that this is not an emergency route. Safeguarding is out of MVP, there is presently nowhere else for such a report to go, and nothing describes what the Principal does with one — where a child is in danger now, the family should speak to the school directly and, where needed, the appropriate authorities (BR-4, OQ-2).
Offer only the guardian's own children. A complaint concerning another family's child cannot be raised here at all (BR-8, A2).
Say who holds it once it is raised. That is the whole purpose of the acknowledgement — a complaint being worked and one that has been forgotten must not look the same (BR-5).

operations.writesOnRead: Opening a student record writes an audit entry naming the actor, the student and the time, because this reaches a child's personal data. A read that is never shown has still recorded the opening.

planningRules.rule: Report only the fields that came back, and never fill a gap. A field absent from the response is absent because the role may not see it — an identity number for a Teacher, medical information for anyone (BR-7, BR-9). Supplying it from an earlier read, from the search result, or from anywhere else defeats the filtering entirely.

Never resolve an ambiguous name to the likelier student. This record is the single source of truth and every module keys off it (BR-2); a correction, a message or a fee action taken on the wrong child starts here and is not caught downstream.

Never chain an update onto a read. Reading is a permitted act for eight roles; changing is permitted for three. One plan doing both proposes a change nobody asked for on a record someone only wanted to look at.
Never plan this to enumerate. A record at a time is a read of a person; sweeping a class or a branch through repeated reads writes an audit entry per child and is a list by another name.
branch_id comes from $session. A student at another campus is outside the row scope and returns NOT_IN_SCOPE, which is the correct answer, not a reason to widen anything.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse. The audit entry it writes is deliberate and never editable under the audit-trail convention — the controller must not attempt to remove it.

plan.atomicity: Two different guarantees, and they matter separately. planningRules.rule: Report the counts before the plan is emitted, and never run a batch the actor has not seen the size of. This creates student records, guardian portal accounts and fee liability for a whole cohort at once, and none of it can be uncreated.

Never re-run a batch to retry the rejected rows. Re-running recognises what already succeeded and skips it (BR-13), but the rejected rows are still rejected — they need correcting in the file and re-uploading, which is a screen act.

Never plan an import to add one student, or a handful. This path exists deliberately outside the inquiry, approval and test (BR-1); using it for a child who should go through admission bypasses every check that pipeline exists to make.

planningRules.rule: Never supply an amount the request did not state. A price list is what every family is billed from, and a figure a planner chose becomes real money on somebody's invoice.

planningRules.rule: Never supply, adjust or round an amount. Every figure on an invoice is calculated by the API in one fixed order — structure, less concession, less credit, split by installment, plus late fee, plus tax (BR-1, BR-2) — and a number a planner supplies is money charged to a family that no rule produced.
Never supply the issue date or the due date. Overdue tracking and any late fee run from the due date (BR-7 of UC-04-15), so a date invented here decides when families start being chased and fined.
Never chain an issue onto a preview. The preview is what the office checks before charging anybody; a plan that previews and issues in one run removes the check the two-step shape exists to provide.

Report the excluded students by name and reason. A student with no approved structure, not yet placed, or already billed for the period is excluded and listed rather than aborting the run (BR-3, BR-12, BR-14) — and a preview reported as a clean total hides them.
Never approve a structure to make a preview complete. NO_APPROVED_STRUCTURE means the price list for that class has not been agreed, which is a decision by a different person under UC-04-01.

plan.atomicity: Two guarantees, and they matter separately. **Per student it is atomic**: the invoice, its lines, the credit drawdown, the concession drawdown and the ledger postings are all created or none are, so a credit is never consumed without a bill to show for it (BR-15, E7). **The batch is not**: a student whose posting fails is listed and the rest are issued. planningRules.rule: Never type a figure onto a challan. Every amount, the due date and the after-due-date amount are taken from the invoice so the slip and the ledger cannot disagree (BR-2), and there is no parameter for any of them.
Never treat a reprint as a new challan. Reprinting returns the same reference (BR-7); two references for one bill is how a payment gets entered twice, and the bank quotes whichever slip it is handed.

Never combine invoices onto one slip. One challan covers one invoice, because one reference has to tie the bank payment back to the exact invoice (BR-3, BR-4) — a combined slip returns one total that could only be split across invoices by guessing, which UC-04-05 BR-3 forbids outright.

Prefer a batch scope over a class scope, and report the periods when a class scope is used. A batch is one issue run and so one period; a class may hold unpaid invoices from several, and printing them all hands a family three slips they did not expect.
Never generate a challan for a paid or cancelled invoice to 'have one on file'. A family holding a slip will take it to the bank, and E1 and E2 refuse it for that reason.
Never chain a payment record onto a challan. Printing moves no money (BR-9); the payment is recorded when the stamped school copy comes back, which may be days later.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. plan.atomicity: One write, and the tightest atomicity in the module: the payment, the receipt and both ledger postings are created together or not at all. Receipt numbers are gapless and never reused, and a failed entry consumes none (BR-7). The receipt goes to the guardian at the point of recording and does not block (E9). returns.description: The payment as recorded, with its receipt.

errors.meaning: The challan reference matches no challan.
errors.note: Message: "No challan matches that reference. Check the stamped copy." Never guess the invoice — a guess credits the wrong family (BR-3).

errors.meaning: The invoice has already been paid in full.
errors.note: The message names the settling receipt. Money arriving against a settled invoice is an unallocated receipt, not a second payment.

errors.meaning: The amount is greater than the outstanding balance.
errors.note: An overpayment is refused rather than creating a negative balance (BR-6). Never reduce the amount to fit — the money that arrived is what it is.

errors.meaning: The amount is zero or negative.
The payment date is in the future.
The ledger posting failed.
errors.written: Nothing. No payment, no receipt, no posting (BR-9).
errors.note: Message: "The payment could not be recorded. Nothing has been saved." No receipt number is consumed (BR-7).

errors.meaning: An online confirmation arrived twice for the same transaction reference.
errors.written: Nothing new. The original payment stands.
errors.note: The message names the existing receipt. A gateway retrying its callback must not credit an invoice twice (UC-04-03 BR-11).

errors.meaning: An attempt was made to edit a recorded payment.
errors.note: A recorded payment is never edited (BR-10). Correcting it is UC-04-12, which reverses the entry and records a new one with a reason.

errors.meaning: The receipt message to the guardian failed.
errors.written: The payment, the receipt and the postings all stand.
errors.notWritten: The guardian has not been sent the receipt.
errors.note: Report both halves. The payer does not hold proof.

planningRules.rule: Never supply, round or adjust the amount. It is the money that physically arrived, and E3 refusing an amount above the balance is not a prompt to reduce it — an overpayment means the family paid more than the bill, which is a fact somebody has to deal with, not a number to trim.

Never guess which invoice the money is for. A bank payment with no matching challan reference records nothing, because a guess credits the wrong family and the error surfaces months later as a family chased for a fee they paid (BR-3, E1).

Never default the payment date to today. It is when the money was received, not when it was keyed — a challan paid on Friday and entered on Monday is dated Friday, or the day's collection figure is wrong (BR-4).
Never key an online payment. A gateway-confirmed payment is recorded automatically with no keying (BR-8), and entering one by hand risks recording it twice under a second receipt number.
Never edit or re-record a payment to correct it. A recorded payment is never edited (BR-10, E8); correcting it is UC-04-12, which reverses the entry and records a new one with a reason.

Never absorb unidentified money into the nearest invoice. Money received without an invoice to apply it to is held as an unallocated receipt and reported (BR-1) — putting it somewhere plausible is how a family ends up credited for someone else's payment.
Report the receipt delivery separately from the payment. The payment stands even where the receipt did not reach the guardian (E9), and a payer without proof will ask again.
branch_id and session_id come from $session.

reversal.statement: fee.payment.correction.raise, under UC-04-12. A recorded payment is never deleted or edited — the correction reverses the entry, records a new one on the correct account with a reason, supersedes the receipt and restores the invoice statuses. It is an approved act somebody decides on, never a compensating call the controller makes after a failure.

The list exceeds the display threshold.

planningRules.rule: Never supply an amount or an age. Both are calculated as billed less paid and due date to today (BR-3, BR-4); a figure held anywhere else drifts from the ledger, which is exactly what BR-4 forbids.
Never set include_students_on_a_plan to widen a list. A family paying as agreed must not be chased (BR-2), and a longer list is not a better one.
Never chain a reminder onto the list. Running it sends nothing (BR-10), and who gets chased is a decision somebody takes after reading it.
Report the run time with the total, and say so where the list ran during an invoice batch. The figure is a position at a moment, and BR-5 means it moves as payments come in.
Never treat an empty list as a failure. No overdue fees is the answer the school wants (E1).

operations.name: fee.reminder.send
operations.idempotencyKey: student_ids + template_id + channel + the send timestamp, so a repeat does not message the same families twice and inflate the reminder history BR-12 reads
operations.purpose: Send a templated fee reminder to selected families, resolving each family's own figures, and log every send against the student.

parameters.name: student_ids

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No overdue student matches, or none holding a contact for that channel.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates. For a set, report how many and who before anything is sent — a reminder cannot be unsent.

parameters.notes: The families to remind, drawn from the overdue list. Families meeting an approved installment plan are excluded and cannot be re-added by selecting all (BR-3); a family who has missed an installment is not excluded (BR-4).

parameters.name: channel
parameters.notes: Only channels the student record holds a contact for are offered (BR-5).

parameters.name: template_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No reminder template of that name for this channel.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates.

parameters.notes: A saved reminder template. Required for a send to more than one family (BR-6, E3). Omit only for a single family written to directly.

parameters.name: message_body
parameters.notes: Maximum 1000 characters, for one family only. Never for several — free text to many cannot be reviewed before it goes or reused after (BR-6).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: sent
fields.description: student_id, reminder_id, outstanding_at_send, delivery_status. Queued until the provider says otherwise (BR-8).

fields.name: failed
fields.description: student_id and the reason.

fields.name: excluded_on_plan
fields.description: Families meeting an approved plan, kept out of the send (BR-3).

fields.name: excluded_paid
fields.description: Families who paid since the list was run (E6). Not chased.

fields.name: no_contact
fields.description: Families holding no contact for the channel (E1).

fields.name: recently_reminded
fields.description: Families reminded within the configured interval, flagged so the same family is not messaged three times in a week (BR-12).

fields.name: awaiting_authorisation
fields.description: True where the selection exceeded the threshold. Nothing has been sent (BR-7).

errors.meaning: Some selected students hold no contact for any channel.
errors.note: Listed. Adding a contact is a correction to the student record (UC-03-01).

errors.meaning: A template field cannot be filled for a family.
errors.note: The send is blocked rather than going out with a gap where the amount should be. Never fill it in by hand (BR-2).

errors.meaning: A multi-family send was attempted with free text.
The selection is above the threshold.
errors.written: The send is queued and School Admin is notified.
errors.note: Not a failure. Never split the selection to get under the threshold.

errors.meaning: There is no messaging balance for the channel.
errors.note: Never fall back to another channel — the family may hold no contact for it (BR-5).

errors.meaning: Some selected families have paid since the list was run.
errors.note: Listed and skipped. A family who paid this morning is not chased this afternoon (UC-04-06 BR-5).

errors.meaning: A Staff user attempted to send a reminder.
errors.note: Only Accounts send fee reminders (BR-1). In practice the capability is absent from a Staff allow-list.

errors.meaning: The provider cannot be reached.
errors.note: Report them as queued, never as sent (BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Report what a set resolves to before anything is sent, with the count and the total outstanding. A reminder cannot be unsent, and "sab ko bhej do" is a phrase with no number in it.

Never supply an amount or a due date into a message. Each reminder carries that family's own figures, filled from their invoice — a figure typed into a message is a figure that can be wrong (BR-2), and it is the number the family will act on.

Never include families meeting an approved plan. They are excluded by the API and cannot be re-added by selecting all (BR-3); a family paying as agreed being chased is the failure that rule exists to prevent.
Never split a selection to get under the authorisation threshold. It exists so a School Admin sees a large chase before it goes (BR-7).
Never switch channel because one has no balance or no contact. The channel was chosen, and a family who gave a number and no email is not reachable by email (BR-5).

Report reminders as queued, never as delivered, and report the recently-reminded flag. The school believing a family was told when they were not is what BR-8 prevents, and messaging the same family three times in a week is what BR-12 prevents.
Never claim a reminder does anything to the debt. It charges no late fee, alters no invoice and extends no due date (BR-10).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A reminder cannot be unsent. The log entry, the amount held against it and the delivery status are history. Where the wrong families were chased, the answer is an apology somebody sends, not a compensating call.

operations.name: fee.cancellation.raise
operations.idempotencyKey: invoice_id or batch_id, since one invoice carries one open cancellation at a time
operations.purpose: Raise a cancellation proposal against an unpaid invoice, or a whole batch raised in error, with the reason and a written description.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.notes: One invoice, or a whole batch raised in error (BR-8).

parameters.name: invoice_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No unpaid issued invoice matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, period and amount.

parameters.notes: Required where the scope is Invoice. Must carry no payment (BR-2, E1).

parameters.type: enum: Billed to the wrong student | Wrong amount | Wrong billing period | Duplicate of another invoice | Student had left | Structure applied in error | Other
parameters.notes: Why the charge should not have been raised (BR-4). Read from what the actor stated, never chosen to fit.

parameters.name: description
parameters.notes: 20 to 500 characters. What actually went wrong, in terms a reader can follow (BR-4, E2). The actor's own words — an invoice that disappeared with no explanation is the thing an auditor asks about first.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: cancellation_id
fields.description: The proposal.

fields.description: Awaiting approval. Nothing is cancelled yet.

fields.name: amount_to_cancel
fields.description: The invoice's outstanding amount. Never typed and never partial (BR-3).

fields.name: invoice_count
fields.description: For a batch scope, how many invoices would be cancelled.

fields.name: paid_invoices
fields.description: For a batch scope, those that have been paid and will be refused (BR-8, E7). Shown now so the approver knows.

fields.name: concession_to_return
fields.description: Concession the invoice consumed, returned on approval (BR-7).

fields.name: credit_to_return
fields.description: Family credit the invoice consumed, returned on approval (BR-7).

fields.name: raised_by
fields.description: The acting user, who may not also approve it (BR-1).

errors.meaning: A payment has been recorded against the invoice.
errors.note: The message names the amount and date. This is a credit, not a cancellation (BR-2) — the school is holding the family's money.

errors.meaning: No reason or description was given.
errors.note: Message: "Describe what went wrong. A cancelled charge has to be explainable." Ask; never compose one.

errors.meaning: The invoice has already been cancelled.
The invoice has been written off.
errors.note: A written-off debt is a recognised loss on a correct charge. Cancelling it would say the charge was wrong, which is a different statement.

errors.meaning: Some invoices in the batch have been paid.
errors.written: The proposal covers the unpaid ones.
errors.note: Listed. Those need a credit under UC-04-10, which is a separate decision (BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Never compose the description. An invoice that disappeared with no explanation is the thing an auditor asks about first (BR-4), and a description a planner wrote explains what it guessed rather than what went wrong.
Never choose the reason to fit. It is a fixed list read for patterns afterwards; "Other" used as a default makes the list stop meaning anything, and a wrong code hides a recurring billing fault.

Never use a cancellation where money has been received. E1 is BR-2 working — the school is holding the family's money, and cancelling the bill would leave the payment with nothing to sit against. That is a credit under UC-04-10.
Never chain the approval. A cancellation is raised by one person and approved by another, because a charge that can be raised and removed by one hand is not a control (BR-1).
Never chain a corrected invoice onto a cancellation. Cancelling raises nothing in its place; the correct charge goes through the ordinary run as a separate, deliberate act (BR-10).
Report the paid invoices in a batch proposal. They will be refused (BR-8), and the approver needs to know that approving this cancels 18 of 20 rather than all of them.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A proposal is not withdrawn by anything written here — it is approved or returned by the School Admin. Nothing has been cancelled and no family has been told, so an unwanted proposal simply is not approved. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

steps.note: One step, and it is the act that withdraws the charge. The balancing entry posts, the invoice moves to Cancelled, any concession or family credit it consumed is returned, and the family is told.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the acting user raised the proposal themselves, and whether the ledger posting succeeds, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval, the balancing ledger entry, the invoice's status, the returned concession and credit, and the audit entry together or not at all (E6). Nothing is deleted and nothing is edited — the original entry stays in place, so the books show both what was billed and what was withdrawn (BR-5, BR-6). Where the original accounting period has closed, the entry posts to the current open one; a closed period is not reopened to tidy a mistake (BR-9). The invoice leaves overdue tracking and stops accruing late fee at once (BR-12). The message to the family is separate and does not block (E8) — but it matters, because a challan already in their hands must not be paid by mistake (BR-11).

operations.name: fee.cancellation.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: cancellation_id, since a proposal carries one approval
operations.purpose: Approve a cancellation, post the balancing entry, mark the invoice cancelled, return what it consumed and tell the family.

parameters.name: cancellation_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No cancellation proposal matches awaiting a decision.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, invoice, amount and who raised it.

parameters.notes: The cancellation proposal, resolved from how the actor named it — the reference, or the student and invoice.

parameters.name: branch_id

planningRules.rule: Never carry last period's actual into a figure. It is offered as a starting point, not applied as one — a budget that repeats what happened is a forecast nobody made.
Never supply a figure the request did not state. A budget is what somebody is measured against (BR-8), and a number a planner filled in measures them against nothing they agreed.

Never mark a closed day. A day the school was shut is not a day anybody was absent (BR-3), and E2 refusing it is the calendar doing its job — never move the date to the nearest open day.

Never overwrite a pre-applied leave mark. Approved leave is applied to the roster before marking begins (BR-6) precisely so a child on sanctioned leave is not marked absent, and replacing it undoes a decision somebody made.
Never re-emit after ALREADY_MARKED. A register already saved is corrected with a reason, and the original mark stays visible (BR-7) — saving again would be a second register for one day.
Never chain an alert onto marking. Absences feed the alert route but a person decides when a family is told (BR-9), and a parent messaged automatically is one the school did not choose to message.
